boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Georgetown study environments, from open reading rooms and silent floors to reservable collaboration spaces and specialized libraries.

cards.title: Settle Into a Potomac-View Carrel
cards.subtitle: Open carrels and lounge seating on Georgetown's Hilltop Campus
cards.notes: Choose a carrel for focused reading or a lounge seat for a wider view; check current library hours before heading over.
cards.short_summary: The main campus library pairs open study areas with quiet accommodations and city-facing lounge views.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgetown states that Lauinger Library has open carrels on every floor and lounge areas with views of Washington and the Potomac River.
cards.access_notes: Located at 37th and Prospect Streets NW. Consult the library's current hours page before visiting; overnight admission restrictions may apply.

cards.title: Spread Out in Pierce Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Flexible tables, varied seating, and reservable rooms on Lauinger's third floor
cards.notes: Use the open area for solo or group work, or reserve an enclosed room when conversation and shared screens matter.
cards.short_summary: A renovated reading room that supports open study, group sessions, and technology-intensive scholarship.
cards.evidence_claim: The majority of Pierce Reading Room is a first-come, first-served open study area with multiple table and seating types; it also contains two reservable group rooms.
cards.access_notes: Lauinger Library, third floor. The open area enters a Go Quiet period daily from 10 p.m. to 8 a.m.; enclosed rooms may be reserved up to 10 days ahead for up to three hours daily.

cards.title: Plug Into a Larger Screen
cards.subtitle: A private, no-reservation workspace inside the Gelardin Center
cards.notes: Bring your own device and connect to the room's large monitor; keep the visit within the posted three-hour daily limit.
cards.short_summary: A quiet single-room option for large-screen project work or a brief private video call.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgetown describes the Quiet Room as a quiet space with a large monitor and keyboard for connecting a personal device; no reservation is required.
cards.access_notes: Inside the Gelardin Center on Lauinger Library's first floor. No reservation is required, but use is limited to no more than three hours per day.

cards.title: Build a Work Session Around the Second Floor
cards.subtitle: Discussion tables, reservable rooms, and the library's designated food floor
cards.notes: Pick a lounge table when discussion is useful, then shift to a reservable room if the project needs a closed workspace.
cards.short_summary: A collaboration-oriented floor with extensive room inventory and the library's only permitted food area.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgetown identifies most of Lauinger's second floor as a study lounge and lists numerous reservable and first-come, first-served study rooms there.
cards.access_notes: Lauinger Library, second floor. Room eligibility and reservation rules vary; ten small group rooms are listed as first-come, first-served.

cards.title: Use the Graduate-Only Quiet Lounge
cards.subtitle: A GOCard-access study room reserved for graduate students
cards.notes: Bring your GOCard and choose this lounge when you need quiet work with laptop use permitted and graduate-only access.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated quiet lounge that separates graduate study from Lauinger's more conversational areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The library lists a Graduate Study Lounge on Lauinger's first floor that is designated quiet, permits laptops, requires GOCard entry, and is solely for graduate students.
cards.access_notes: Lauinger Library, first floor. Access is limited to graduate students and requires a GOCard swipe; available whenever the library is open.

cards.title: Find Quiet on Lauinger's Fourth Floor
cards.subtitle: A Main Campus graduate lounge with controlled entry
cards.notes: Use this room for laptop-based quiet study, and have your GOCard ready because access is restricted at the door.
cards.short_summary: A controlled-access quiet room specifically designated for Main Campus graduate students.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgetown states that the fourth-floor Graduate Study Lounge is quiet, permits laptop use, requires GOCard entry, and is limited to Main Campus graduate students.
cards.access_notes: Lauinger Library, fourth floor. Limited to Main Campus graduate students, with GOCard swipe required; available during library hours.

cards.title: Take Technical Work to Blommer
cards.subtitle: A quiet science library inside the Reiss Science Building
cards.notes: Head to Reiss for a quiet session near science collections, or reserve Blommer's group room for collaborative work.
cards.short_summary: A discipline-focused library combining silent-study expectations with a reservable collaboration room.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgetown designates Blommer Science Library as a quiet study area and lists a reservable group study room there for up to eight people.
cards.access_notes: Located on the third floor of Reiss Science Building. Quiet-area rules prohibit talking or playing music, including through headphones; consult current hours before visiting.

cards.title: Read in Healy's Silent Bioethics Library
cards.subtitle: An entire specialized library designated for quiet study
cards.notes: Bring reading-heavy work and observe the library-wide quiet rule; use the accessible entrance through Maguire Hall if needed.
cards.short_summary: A specialized collection and study environment where quiet rules cover the entire library.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgetown identifies the entire Bioethics Research Library as a quiet study area and locates it in Healy Hall, room 102.
cards.access_notes: Healy Hall, room 102. Quiet-study rules apply throughout. The accessible route enters through Maguire Hall; the mezzanine is not accessible.

cards.title: Bring a Full Project Team to the Millennium Room
cards.subtitle: Lauinger's largest listed group study room
cards.notes: Reserve this room for a larger team and connect a laptop to the wall display; arrive promptly to protect the booking.
cards.short_summary: A ten-person collaboration room equipped with Lauinger's largest listed study-room display.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgetown lists the Millennium Room as its largest Hilltop group study room, accommodating up to ten people and providing a 50-inch LCD display.
cards.access_notes: Advance reservations are limited to eligible Hilltop community members. Rooms are booked in one-hour segments, and a reservation is forfeited after 15 minutes if the group has not arrived.

cards.title: Scale Up a Data-Heavy Research Session
cards.subtitle: A technology-enabled lab inside Pierce Reading Room
cards.notes: Use this lab for computational or visualization work only after confirming eligibility and securing the required reservation.
cards.short_summary: A specialized environment for research teams working with computation, data, and large-scale visualization.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgetown describes the Duran Visualization and Learning Lab as a technology-enabled space reservable for instructional sessions or computational and data-intensive research and visualization.
cards.access_notes: Inside Pierce Reading Room on Lauinger's third floor. Faculty, staff, and research teams may reserve it; student requests are evaluated case by case.
